plans.name: Company-first: Token Tails Rescue Rail (a live consumer app, plus its new in-window payout rail on Tempo, Arbitrum, Base and Arc)
plans.thesis:
Pitch Token Tails as a company that already ships to consumers. It has a web app, iOS and Android. Its historical peaks are 542k registered users (all-time, including legacy accounts from a retired channel) and 307.6k web MAU. It took 1st place at the Bybit Blockchain-for-Good forum, which is used only as a credential; the BGA program itself is excluded. The new work in the window becomes that company's next product: ShelterSplit real payouts to a named shelter, shown on a public transparency page inside tokentails.com, with Catnip Heist as the consumer front door.

What I re-verified today and what it changes. The official Colosseum World's Fair rules PDF (fetched 2026-09-28, section 14) lists ecosystem tracks with paid slots:
- Tempo: $100k over 10 prizes.
- Arbitrum: $25k over 5.
- Base: $25k over 5.
- General pool: 20 prizes of $15k, plus the $30k grand prize, $5k Public Goods and $5k University.

The earlier strategy proof (P≈2%) only counted the general pool. Tempo is Stripe and Paradigm's payments-first L1. It pays gas in USD stablecoins, and its mainnet has been live since 2026-03-18 (chain 4217, verified). ShelterSplit already has 8 TIP-20 compatibility tests (transferWithMemo, pause, blacklist). So the Tempo track is the single best-fitting paid slot pool in the whole search. Arc Microgrants remains the highest-P single entry.

What limits the company pitch:
- Colosseum states that "products are judged only on the work completed between the competition's start and end dates". The legacy app therefore counts as founder-market fit, distribution and team execution, not as the judged product. The judged product must be the new rail and the heist, both created after Sep 14 (file birth dates are Sep 25 and Sep 28).
- Pre-existing code must be disclosed.
- Traction must be labelled honestly everywhere: "historical peaks". On-chain activity was on SEI, not Stellar, and it stopped in March 2026. extra/traction.md currently cites the SEI Dune dashboard as if it were Stellar, and that must be fixed before anything is submitted.
- Programs that score traction (Colosseum's hackathon page, Circle, Arbitrum Dubai "bring an existing product") are where the company pitch adds fit. Arc says "promise counts for more than traction", so there the pitch adds little.

Honest bottom line:
- P(at least one cash win) ≈ 0.36 with Anitya as an uncorrelated diversifier, or about 0.29 crypto-only.
- If current, verifiable traction numbers are supplied, it rises to about 0.40.
- The range is 0.25–0.45, because the Tempo, Arbitrum, Base, Arc, Avalanche and Circle entrant counts are unpublished assumptions.
- No single entry exceeds about 18%. Expected cash is about $2.4k.

entries.rubricFit:
Official rules section 8 (unweighted), simulated judge scores out of 5:
- (a) Functionality and code quality: 4. It has 41 contract tests plus 120 heist tests, mainnet deploys on 3 chains and a live payout. It would be 2 without the payout.
- (b) Potential impact/TAM: 3. Pet and animal-welfare giving is a real consumer market, but no sourced TAM figure is in the repo, so the AI must cite a real source or omit it. The ecosystem impact is modest.
- (c) Novelty: 3. Charity splitters exist. What is new is embedding the splitter in a game with a consumer audience.
- (d) UX: 3. Users never touch a wallet, and the rail is invisible behind the app. Judges may see that as good UX or as a thin blockchain use.
- (e) Open-source and composability: 4. It is MIT, has no dependencies, and uses the TIP-20 and USDC primitives.
- (f) Business plan and ability to execute: 4. This is where the company pitch pays: a live product on 3 platforms and a shipped history.
- Hackathon page's 'Traction' criterion: 2 on historical peaks only. It becomes 3–4 if a current 30-day MAU, revenue or USD sent to shelters is supplied.

Track fit:
- Tempo: strong. It is a payments-first chain and gas is paid in stablecoins.
- Arbitrum: medium.
- Base: weak-medium, as it is a crowded consumer track.

Past-winner pattern: general-pool winners are infra, DeFi and payments, and games rarely win. The rail framing matches 'payments' better than the game does.
entries.pArithmetic:
Per-slot pools. The rules give the slot counts. Entrant counts per track are NOT published, and the ones below are my assumptions.
- General: 23 paid / ~1,250 submissions, from history of 1.0–2.8% = 0.018, x fit 1.1 (company and business-plan strength), which gives 0.02.
- Tempo: 10 slots / assumed ~150 Tempo-integrating entries = 0.067, x fit 1.15 (native TIP-20 memo payouts on a payments chain) = 0.077.
- Arbitrum: 5 / assumed ~100 = 0.05, x 1.0 = 0.05.
- Base: 5 / assumed ~200 = 0.025, x 1.0 = 0.025.
- Independent: 1 - (0.98 x 0.923 x 0.95 x 0.975) = 1 - 0.838 = 0.162.
- The same judges and the same submission make these correlated, so I apply x0.8, which gives ≈0.13.
- Range 0.06–0.20. The biggest unknowns: whether one project may place in several ecosystem tracks (not stated in the rules; a person should ask on the Colosseum Discord), and the size of the Tempo field.

plans.risks:
1. Colosseum judges only in-window work. The legacy app is context, not the scored product. Overselling it as the submission, or failing to disclose pre-existing code, risks disqualification (rules section 13 and the misrepresentation clause).

2. The traction claims are the biggest reputational risk.
- Every figure is a historical peak with no date.
- The on-chain '324k MAU and 659k weekly tx' figure is from a SEI Dune dashboard, and SEI activity stopped in March 2026.
- Citing it as Stellar, or as current, would be misrepresentation.
- Label everything 'historical peak (month, source)' and fix extra/traction.md and ProofSection.tsx before submitting. That fix changes user-facing code, so it must be surfaced to the user, not done silently.

3. Unpublished denominators. Entrant counts for the Tempo, Arbitrum and Base tracks, Arc, Circle and Team1 are my assumptions, so every P has a range of about x0.5 to x1.6. It is unknown whether one project can place in several Colosseum ecosystem tracks; a person must ask on the Colosseum Discord.

4. Correlation. Five of the six entries use the same rail, so if judges see it as 'thin charity splitter' they all fail together. The x0.8 haircut reflects this, and Anitya is the only independent bet.

5. The shelter payout depends on one shelter agreeing, which only a person can arrange. Without it, Arc drops to about 0.15, Colosseum Functionality to 2/5, and Circle to about 0.02.

6. Mainnet signing is irreversible. The framework never signs. Run DRY_RUN, keep balances minimal, and move ownership to a Safe after the payout. Known contract issues elsewhere (the open Stellar mint in docs/CONTRACTS.md) are not fixed by this work; mention them if judges ask.

7. Payee and KYC.
- Colosseum pays an individual Team Leader, possibly in the Phantom CASH stablecoin for the grand prize, and requires prize-acceptance documents and due diligence.
- Arc and Circle pay USDC, with sanctions screening.
- Tax reporting falls on the winner.
- Lithuania is not on the Colosseum exclusion list.

8. Arbitrum Dubai criteria and prizes are 'TBD' and 'may be subject to change', and HackQuest does not judge.

9. Anitya: 2 of 4 past jams published no ranking. Payout method, AI-asset policy and Lithuania payout are unverified.

10. The Tempo mainnet deploy needs Tempo's fee-token semantics (there is no native gas). It is tested only with a TIP-20 mock (Tip20Compat.t.sol), not yet on a live chain. Run DRY_RUN against rpc.tempo.xyz first.

11. The Colosseum deadline is 14 days away, and the videos plus the deploy wave are on the critical path. If the deploy slips past Oct 10, drop Base and submit Tempo plus Arbitrum only.

12. Excluded programs stay excluded: BGA as a program, Mantle, SCF, Giveth, Game3, Taiko, Solana/Superteam (including Colosseum's Solana track), the LT travel subsidy, SDF Marketing and Talent Protocol. Mezo is dropped because it pays in tokens. Base Batches 2026 is closed (applications ran Feb 17 – Mar 9, and demo day is in person in SF).

plans.name: ARC-FIRST, PROOF OVER PROMISE: one real shelter payout on Arc mainnet, reused for every other stablecoin program
plans.thesis:
Put all the human effort into one Arc Microgrants entry that is clearly ahead of the other splitter entries. Then reuse the same deployed and proven contract, the same demo page and the same video for the other stablecoin programs, where it costs little to enter.

Why Arc first:
- It is the only program above 10%.
- Its hard gate (deployed and working on Arc mainnet, plus a public repo) removes many entrants. Re-verified 2026-09-28: 20 x 500 USDC, closes 2026-10-14 23:59 ET, reviewed on a rolling basis in batches, all decisions by 2026-10-21.
- The criteria reward exactly what a proof shows: "Relevance to Arc, technical credibility, the quality of what you built, and whether the project is worth taking further. Promise counts for more than traction here."

The threat is that the splitter niche is already taken. arc-split, splitpay-arc and arcdrip are live on Arc mainnet, per applications/arc-microgrants/notes/win-review.md. So the entry must win on three things the others lack:

(1) An Arc-only mechanism. Arc's native gas token is USDC ("the same balance" as the ERC-20 at 0x3600...0000, per docs.arc.io/connect-to-arc and evm-differences). So add a payable receive/donate path to ShelterSplit: anyone sends plain USDC to the contract address and it is split to shelters on arrival. There is no approve step and no second gas token, and the shelter never needs to hold anything but USDC. This is impossible with USDC on other EVM chains. Arc's deterministic finality on inclusion also gives an instant receipt.

(2) A second live instance in EURC (0xbEf5...21c1 on Arc per docs.arc.io/contract-addresses). A Lithuanian team can pay EU shelters in euros using the same contract.

(3) A real, named shelter that agreed in writing and publishes its own wallet. It gets a public mainnet disbursement tx, and real third-party donor txs follow from one post by the existing @tokentails account.

After that, the proof feeds these programs:
- Colosseum World's Fair. New finding in the rules PDF: the Tempo track pays $100k across 10 products (s.14(f)). ShelterSplit already has 8 TIP-20 compatibility tests, and the earlier estimate of 2% looked only at the general pool.
- Team1 Avalanche and Circle Developer Grants: both rolling.
- Arbitrum Dubai: Nov 16 - Dec 6.
- Optionally, Anitya World Jam: an uncorrelated diversifier on a different asset.

Every number is base rate x fit. Base rates marked "assumed" are not published by the programs.

- C1 Relevance to Arc, 8/10: the native-USDC auto-split exists only on Arc, USDC is the gas token so shelters need nothing else, the EURC instance, and finality-based receipts. Competing splitters score about 5, because theirs are generic ERC-20 splitters that work on any chain.

plans.name: Game-First: Catnip Heist Engine Sprint (Anitya stack + AI-allowed jams + two big-ticket platform contests)
plans.thesis:
Nearly every Halloween or stealth jam fails for this team, and live pages confirm why. The team uses AI for about 90% of the work, and these jams ban it: Terror Jam 2026 disqualifies any game "found to use AI". Scream Jam, Comfy Jam, Cookie Jam #5, RGDC, UNIDOS, Pixel Forge and Month of Horror all ban generative AI. Eclipse bars "substantially AI-generated end-to-end entries" from prizes. So the game-first path only works where AI is allowed and where a new game built on an existing engine, or an adapted existing game, is eligible. Five places qualify, all verified on 2026-09-28.

(1) Anitya, three ways to win. The weekly challenges have tiny fields: "Story to Playable" pays 2 x $50, has 3 entries so far and closes Sep 30. The later weekly and surprise challenges share a $600 pool. The main World Jam pays $1,000, $700 and $400 and closes Oct 21. All three use GLB-exported Catnip Heist voxel cats, dogs and props. Anitya bans no AI and says GLB files import directly.
(2) Bezi Jam 14, "Something Wicked". It is a Halloween jam where you should "make us afraid of the dark", which suits a lights-out stealth game. AI is banned only for fan art, and web builds are recommended. It runs Oct 23-26 and pays $150, $100, $50 and $50.
(3) Game Gauntlet SIM Jam. It lists "immersive sim" as a genre, allows AI with disclosure, and allows pre-existing engines and frameworks. It pays $1,000 and $500 and closes Nov 4.
(4) Meta VR Start Developer Competition 2026. It has an "Adapted/Significantly Updated" division that takes a pre-existing project with a new platform integration, allows WebXR through the Immersive Web SDK, sets no AI ban, admits organisations, and excludes only Brazil, Quebec and sanctioned regions. The pool is $1M across 20 awards, and it closes Nov 18. Catnip Heist becomes a hands-first mixed-reality tabletop diorama; src/render/diorama.ts already exists.
(5) Amazon Developer Hackathon, Fire TV track. Web tech is allowed, the Fire TV or Vega simulator is enough, existing projects must be "significantly updated", and organisations may enter. Prizes are $25k, $15k and $4k, and it closes Oct 23. The entry is couch co-op Catnip Heist: 7 of the 8 levels need both cats, so each cat gets its own pad. Gamepad and D-pad support already exist.

Shared first step (AI does it, a human approves the push): commit catnip-heist/, fix the failing retry-leak e2e test (e2e/heist.spec.ts:348), deploy the dist/ build statically, and write a GLTFExporter script that dumps every voxel actor and prop to GLB.

Honest result: P(at least one cash win) ≈ 0.60 (range about 0.40-0.70). Most of that comes from the $50 Anitya weekly prizes and the main Anitya jam, which share organiser and payout risk. P(at least one win of $500 or more) is only about 0.17. EV is about $2,340, and about 85% of it is the 4% Meta shot. Adding Arc Microgrants from STRATEGY-PROOF.md (0.15, a separate asset and separate judges) raises P(at least one) to about 1-(0.398 x 0.85) ≈ 0.66.

plans.name: Shelter Receipts: real shelters paid in USDC on Arc, and every rescued cat linked to a public payout
plans.thesis:
The impact angle scores in only a few places, and they are the same few the earlier analysis found. I re-checked the dedicated impact and animal-welfare funders today (2026-09-28) with WebFetch, and none of them works. Purina BetterWithPets has no open call. Marchig is closed. Pollination and Echoing Green don't fit a for-profit MB. The Devpost "Social Good" hackathons worth real cash (EurekaDev $19k, Neighborhood Hacks $34k) are for high-school students only. Arc Acceleration Season closed on Sep 22 and is for LatAm startups. The Tameion Agents Hackathon on Arc House shows no prize, so I can't count it. So the impact story is best used as the thing that raises fit in programs that are open and pay cash: Arc Microgrants, the Colosseum Public Good and general prizes, Circle Developer Grants, Team1 and Arbitrum Dubai. Anitya is added as the one entry judged on a different asset, which spreads the risk.

The centrepiece is a real shelter partnership. The app already has partner shelters: the CMS has shelter records, and blessings are real rescued cats. The weakness is that the backend generates and holds the shelters' Stellar wallets, so Token Tails holds those keys and a judge would not accept payouts to them as proof of impact. The fix:
1. One (ideally two) named partner shelters each create their own self-custody EVM address.
2. Each signs a short consent to be named and gives a 20-second clip.
3. ShelterSplit is deployed and verified on Arc mainnet, with that shelter registered by basis points.
4. A real USDC disburse() to the shelter produces a public transaction.
5. A public Impact Ledger page, built by AI, reads the Disbursed events and links each payout to the shelter and to its rescued cats in the app.

The pitch everywhere: "Players rescue real shelter cats; shelters get paid on-chain, in a public ledger anyone can audit." On Arc it adds a point only Arc can claim. USDC is Arc's gas token, so a shelter receives, holds and spends one asset and never needs a gas token.

Rules:
- Never claim revenue or shelter totals we can't prove. If the payout is funded by Token Tails rather than real sales, label it "proof payout".
- Replace the peak and SEI-mismatched traction with current figures, or leave the figure out.

Honest outcome: roughly a 1-in-3 chance of at least one cash win, not a sure thing. The most likely win is Arc's $500.

scores.strategy: S1 Company-first: Token Tails Rescue Rail (Tempo/Arbitrum/Base/Arc + Anitya)
scores.entryCorrections: Colosseum 0.13 -> 0.08. The denominator is wrong. The blind judges' '10-15% if all fixes land' has no base rate behind it. General pool: 23/~2,500 = 0.009. The x1.1 'company' fit is not supported, because only in-window work is judged and due diligence will see the filed FY2025 revenue of EUR 105 [F-022]. The Base track '$25k over 5' is NOT in the repo evidence: critCrypto says ecosystem-track amounts are unpublished, and win-review/chain-decision cite only Tempo and Arbitrum from s.14. Count Base as about 0 until the rules PDF quote is recorded. Arbitrum track: rules s.7 allows one project per team and multi-track tagging is unanswered, so apply x0.5, about 0.015. Combined ≈ 0.08 after correlation. Arc 0.15 -> 0.14: repo judges estimate 100-300 entrants, which puts the base at 0.07-0.20, and three splitters (arc-split, splitpay-arc, arcdrip) are already live on mainnet. Arbitrum Dubai 0.065 -> 0.05: the adversarial verdict already cut fit 1.3 to 1.0, and 'existing product allowed' does not lift a users criterion scored on historical peaks. Circle 0.03 -> 0.025, matching the verdict. Team1 0.05 -> 0.04: the program warns of high application volume and no counts are published. Anitya 0.10 kept. Independent crypto ≈ 0.30, correlation-adjusted ≈ 0.25, plus Anitya ≈ 0.30 (range 0.18-0.40). The 0.40 'if traction' figure is not granted: F-001 (542k) is self-reported and unverified, the peaks are undated, and the SEI data is mislabelled.
